name: Elasmosaurus
subjectPrompt: One prehistoric Elasmosaurus marine reptile in a diagonal three-quarter swimming pose. Small wedge-shaped toothed head on an extraordinarily long tapering neck, neck longer than the whole torso and short trailing tail together. Maintain a modest gently flowing neck bend, unlike the tight swan-neck pose. Smooth slate-teal and olive-gray upper skin with pale cream underside and near-subtle mottling, a short robust barrel torso, one continuous tapering short tail, exactly four distinct broad paddle flippers attached at the front and rear of the body. No extra fins on its back or tail and no sea scene. Keep the entire silhouette inside the square, neck reaching to the upper left, torso and flippers diagonally lower right. Anatomically accurate, whole animal.
